answer: The fable multiplier is published, charged in pearl, and yarrow lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2361 identities would post 4475 proofs and burn roughly 50 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
